note: Every email below was read on the source page listed, on the date above. Nothing was guessed or built from a name pattern. list=send means eligible for the gated send list; list=hold means a person to approach by hand or a contact that could not be verified.

candidates.name: Christopher Arris Oakley
candidates.work: Keeping the Circle: American Indian Identity in Eastern North Carolina, 1885 to 2004 (Nebraska, 2005)
candidates.fit: The standard history of eastern North Carolina tribal identity, with the Haliwa Saponi, Lumbee, Coharie, Meherrin, Occaneechi, Tuscarora and Waccamaw Siouan through Jim Crow record keeping.
candidates.hook: Your book Keeping the Circle traces how the Haliwa Saponi and the other eastern North Carolina tribes held on to their identity through the Jim Crow era, when segregated schools and churches carried what the official records would not.

candidates.name: Warren Milteer Jr.
candidates.work: From Indians to Colored People: The Problem of Racial Categories and the Persistence of the Chowans in North Carolina (NCHR, 2016); North Carolina's Free People of Color, 1715 to 1885 (LSU, 2020)
candidates.fit: Writes directly on how North Carolina racial categories reclassified Native people as colored, and on free people of color in northeastern North Carolina counties.
candidates.hook: Your North Carolina Historical Review article From Indians to Colored People follows how shifting racial categories in the records nearly wrote the Chowan people out of North Carolina history.

candidates.name: Malinda Maynor Lowery
candidates.role: Cahoon Family Professor of American History
candidates.work: Lumbee Indians in the Jim Crow South: Race, Identity, and the Making of a Nation (UNC Press, 2010)
candidates.fit: Lumbee historian and filmmaker; her work is the core account of a North Carolina tribe defining itself against a two race legal order.
candidates.hook: Your book Lumbee Indians in the Jim Crow South shows Lumbee people building a nation while the state kept trying to sort them into a two race system.
candidates.subject_topic: Lumbee Indians in the Jim Crow South

candidates.name: Gregory D. Smithers
candidates.work: How Virginia Used Segregation Law to Erase Native Americans (TIME, Made by History, March 2024, with Ashley R. Craig); Native Southerners (Oklahoma, 2019)
candidates.fit: Co-wrote the public history of the 1924 Racial Integrity Act and Plecker's vital records office erasing Virginia Indians on paper.
candidates.hook: Your Made by History essay in TIME with Ashley R. Craig lays out how Virginia used the 1924 Racial Integrity Act and its vital records office to erase Native people on paper.
candidates.subject_topic: your Racial Integrity Act essay in TIME

candidates.name: Stephanie Russo Carroll
candidates.role: Associate Research Professor; Native Nations Institute
candidates.work: CARE Principles for Indigenous Data Governance; Operationalizing the CARE and FAIR Principles for Indigenous data futures (Scientific Data, 2021)
candidates.fit: Leading voice on Indigenous data sovereignty; the right person to say whether a records tool respects tribal authority over Native data.
candidates.hook: The CARE Principles for Indigenous Data Governance, which you led, set the standard any tool touching Native records should meet on collective benefit, authority to control, responsibility and ethics.

candidates.name: Brian Klopotek
candidates.role: Associate Professor, Indigenous, Race, and Ethnic Studies
candidates.work: Recognition Odysseys: Indigeneity, Race, and Federal Tribal Recognition Policy in Three Louisiana Indian Communities (Duke, 2011)
candidates.fit: Studies how race, including Black ancestry, shaped federal recognition of Southern tribes.
candidates.hook: Your book Recognition Odysseys follows three Louisiana Indian communities through federal recognition and shows how ideas about race shaped who the government was willing to call Indian.

candidates.name: Danielle Moretti-Langholtz
candidates.role: Teaching Professor of Anthropology; Director, American Indian Resource Center
candidates.work: Research on the political resurgence of Virginia Indians; Thomasina E. Jordan American Indian Resource Center
candidates.fit: Works with the Virginia tribes whose records Plecker altered and whose recognition followed.
candidates.hook: Your research on the political resurgence of Virginia Indians covers the same communities whose birth and marriage records Walter Plecker's office rewrote.

candidates.name: Tiya Miles
candidates.work: Ties That Bind: The Story of an Afro Cherokee Family in Slavery and Freedom (2005/2015)
candidates.fit: Foremost historian of joined Black and Native family histories.
candidates.hook: Ties That Bind, your history of an Afro Cherokee family in slavery and freedom, reads Black and Native family records together instead of filing them apart.

candidates.name: Kathryn E. Fort
candidates.org: Michigan State University College of Law
candidates.work: MSU Indian Law Clinic (tribal governance and ICWA representation)
candidates.fit: Legal clinic lens on tribal citizenship and records questions.
candidates.hook: The Indian Law Clinic you direct works on exactly the kind of tribal citizenship and records questions where a tool like this would either help or get in the way.

candidates.name: Lawrence T. Locklear
candidates.role: Executive Director, Southeast American Indian Studies
candidates.work: Southeast American Indian Studies and the Curt and Catherine Locklear American Indian Heritage Center
candidates.fit: Leads the main university program for Lumbee and Southeastern Native studies in North Carolina.
candidates.hook: Southeast American Indian Studies at UNC Pembroke works closest to the Lumbee and other Southeastern Native communities most affected by how state records classified race.

candidates.name: Paul Heinegg
candidates.org: Free African Americans of Virginia, North Carolina, South Carolina, Maryland and Delaware
candidates.work: Free African Americans of Virginia, North Carolina, South Carolina, Maryland and Delaware (freeafricanamericans.com)
candidates.fit: The core reference for colonial free families of color in North Carolina and Virginia, many with Native descent claims.
candidates.hook: Your Free African Americans project traces colonial free families of color across Virginia and North Carolina through tax lists, court orders and census returns.

candidates.name: Afro-American Historical and Genealogical Society
candidates.fit: Largest African American genealogy society; reaches researchers who meet reclassified census and vital records daily.
candidates.hook: AAHGS has spent decades helping members trace African American families through census, court and vital records.

candidates.hold_reason: Tribal government. Approach by a personal letter from Matthew, not a demo pitch or an automated send.
